title: Truth over Tricks: Measuring and Mitigating Shortcut Learning in Misinformation Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating detector performance when the correlation between text sentiment (positive/negative/neutral) and authenticity labels differs between training and test sets, and by using LLMs to explicitly inject specific emotional sentiments into text.
Assessing model reliance on stylistic cues by varying the distribution of subjective versus neutral text, and by using LLMs to explicitly inject formal/informal tones or simple/complex word choices.
Creating data splits where the joint distribution of specific topics (e.g., sports, crime, politics) and the ground-truth misinformation labels differs between training and test sets.

Testing models on data splits where the correlation between language perplexity (high versus low token distribution regularities) and authenticity is inverted between training and testing environments.

Prompting LLMs to implicitly rewrite misinformation passages to simulate content authored by specific age demographics (young versus elder) to test if detectors are sensitive to these implicit author attributes.
Prompting LLMs to implicitly rewrite misinformation passages to simulate content authored by specific gender demographics (male versus female) to evaluate changes in detector robustness.
